name: Jacks Back (5 Card Draw)
description: Jacks Back: Five Card Draw with Jacks or Better to open. If no one opens, the same hand is kept and played as ace-to-five lowball, so fewer deals are thrown in. Suited to three to five players.

overview.description: Jacks Back: Five Card Draw with Jacks or Better to open. If no one opens, the same hand is kept and played as ace-to-five lowball, so fewer deals are thrown in. Suited to three to five players.

history.origins: Jacks Back is a draw poker variant that emerged from the Jacks or Better tradition in American home and club play. Five Card Draw with a pair of jacks or better required to open was the dominant form until the spread of Texas Hold'em; Jacks Back adapts that game for smaller groups by keeping the same hand in play when no one opens and switching to ace-to-five lowball, so fewer deals are thrown in. It is documented as a club and home game variant in US poker literature.

setup.players: Two to six players; three to five is ideal so that more hands are played and the Lowball fallback when no one opens is used often.
setup.dealing: Five cards each face down; first betting round requires Jacks or Better to open. If someone opens, draw and second betting round as in Five Card Draw. If no one opens, same hand becomes ace-to-five lowball with a new betting round, then draw for low, then final betting and showdown.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the best high hand at showdown if someone opened the first betting round, or the best low hand (ace-to-five, straights and flushes do not count) if no one opened and the hand was played as lowball.
rules.gameplay: Ante and deal five cards face down to each player. First betting round: Jacks or Better required to open; if no one opens, the hand is not thrown in—players keep their cards and the game switches to ace-to-five lowball with a new betting round begun by the player to dealer's left. If someone opened, play continues as normal Five Card Draw: each active player may discard and draw up to three replacements, then second betting round, then showdown; highest five-card hand wins. If the hand became lowball, after the new betting round players draw to improve for low, then a final betting round; showdown with lowest hand winning (A-2-3-4-5 is best). Often played with a joker as bug for high and fitter for low.
keyRules: Jacks or Better to open first betting round
If no one opens, same hand becomes ace-to-five lowball; new betting round, draw, then final betting and low-hand showdown
If someone opened, standard Five Card Draw: draw, second betting round, high-hand showdown
Standard Five Card Draw hand ranking for high; ace-to-five ranking for low when played as lowball
